COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CRJA No.56 of 2024
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Mayank Joshi, learned legal aid counsel for the 
appellant.
2. Ms. Pushpa Bhatt, learned Deputy Advocate 
General along with Mr. S.C. Dumka, learned AGA with 
Mr. Pramod Tiwari, learned Brief Holder (appeared 
through V.C.) for the State.
3. This appeal has been received from jail through Jailor, 
Sub-Jail, Haldwani against the judgment and order dated 
05.06.2024, passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, 
Khatima in Sessions Trial No.214 of 2021, State vs. Anil 
Saxena, whereby the appellant has been convicted and 
sentenced as under: -
S. 
No.
Conviction Sentence Fine Sentence in￾lieu of fine
1. 304-B IPC 07 years’ R.I. Rs.10,000/- 06 months’ 
additional 
imprisonment
4. Heard on Bail Application (IA No.1/2025).
5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the 
prosecution witnesses, primarily the relatives of the 
deceased, are interested witnesses, and their testimonies 
suffer from material contradictions and improvements. No 
independent witness has been examined to corroborate the 
allegations of dowry harassment, casting serious doubt on 
the prosecution’s version. He further submits that the 
appellant was on bail during the trial and never misused 
the liberty granted to him.
6. Per contra, learned State Counsel opposed the bail 
application on the ground that the deceased was subjected  2
to cruelty and died under unnatural circumstances within 
seven years of marriage. Furthermore, both PW1 and PW2, 
in their statements, confirmed that the deceased was 
harassed by the accused for dowry demands and that the 
accused beat the deceased on 10.08.2021 and 11.08.2021, 
just before her death.
7. Upon hearing the learned counsel for the appellant as 
well as the learned State Counsel and perusal of the 
material on record, this Court is of the considered view that 
the present case does not warrant the grant of bail at this 
stage. The allegations against the appellant are grave and 
serious in nature. The deceased is stated to have died under 
unnatural circumstances within seven years of marriage, 
attracting the presumption under Section 113-B of the 
Indian Evidence Act. The statements of prosecution 
witnesses PW1 and PW2, though related to the deceased, 
are consistent and specific with regard to the harassment 
faced by the deceased at the hands of the accused in 
connection with dowry demands. Accordingly, the bail 
application is dismissed at this stage.
8. List in the month of March, 2026 for final hearing.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
11.09.2025 AK 3

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CRJA No.56 of 2024
Anil Saxena
 --Appellant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand
 --Respondent
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Saurabh Budhori, learned counsel for 
appellant/applicant.
2. Mr. Rakesh Joshi, learned A.G.A. with Mr. 
Manoj Chandra Bhatt, learned Brief Holder for 
the State of Uttarakhand/respondent.
3. Today, the matter is listed on Second Bail 
Application (IA/5/2026) moved by appellant/
applicant for his release on bail.
4. Learned counsel for appellant/applicant 
submits that appellant/applicant is under 
incarceration on his conviction vide judgment 
and order dated 05.06.2024 passed by learned 
Additional Sessions Judge, Khatima, District 
Udham Singh Nagar, in Sessions Trial No.214 
of 2021, State Vs. Anil Saxena, for the offence 
punishable under Section 304B IPC and 
sentenced for 07 years’ R.I. with fine of 
Rs.10,000/- with default stipulation of six 
months additional R.I.
5. He further submits that the cause of 
death of deceased was shown in the post￾mortem report due to haemorrhage and 
shock. He also submits that the appellant/ 
applicant is languishing in jail since 
05.06.2024 and his first bail application was 
rejected by this Court on 11.09.2025.  2
6. Learned State Counsel has filed its 
objection along with delay condonation 
application (IA/6/2026). For the reasons 
indicated in delay condonation application, 
delay in filing the objection is condoned. 
Objection filed by the State is taken on record. 
Delay condonation application (IA/6/2026) 
stands disposed of.
7. Learned State Counsel vehemently 
opposed the second bail application stating 
that there is no new ground taken by 
appellant/applicant in the second bail 
application, he has taken the same ground as 
taken in first bail application. 
8. Having heard learned counsel for the 
parties, this Court is of the view that no new 
ground has been taken by the appellant/
applicant in second bail application and further
the allegations levelled against appellant/
applicant are grave and serious in nature. 
From perusal of the post-mortem report, it is 
found that there are three severe injuries on 
the head due to which haemorrhage and shock 
was occurred and the deceased died, thus, this 
Court is not inclined to grant bail the 
appellant/applicant at this stage.
9. Accordingly, second bail application (IA/
5/2026) is rejected.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 09.04.2026
PN
